nodes.label: docs/canon/REVIEW_WORKLIST.md — one row per claim, ordered by enforcement power. REVIEW_REGISTER.md cuts the pile by file; this one cuts it by claim — the unit that actually costs something, because a claim is what an agent reads and then enforces, and a file is neither true nor false while a claim is. Interpretation, produced 2026-08-04, unreviewed by the user: a list of things to check, not a finding, not a verdict, and not evidence for anything — it appears in its own list as W-E58. Working it is governed by REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md, which is binding: one item at a time, every verdict carrying a command and its pasted output, and no interpretation-tier document — including this one, including CANON_AUDIT.md — ever evidence. Totals: 244 rows, 117 audit-covered, 145 new to this list.

The five tiers plus block decisions, ordered by how much work a wrong claim misdirects before anyone notices — not by how wrong it looks. Tier 1, CLAUDE.md, 50 rows: loads every session for every agent, so a wrong line here is read thousands of times. Tier 2, the 25 live laptop memory files, 70 rows: auto-load every session, same reach as tier 1 with less scrutiny. Tier 3, the 10 .claude/agents/*.md definitions, 50 rows: become hard rules the instant an agent spawns, and the audit found this surface's grounded-to-invented ratio the worst in the repo. Tier 4, v3/README.md, 28 rows: carries a ## Decided heading, which makes every line under it a canon claim. Tier 5, everything else, 40 rows: inert until someone opens it — DESIGN.md + MODEL_CONTRACTS.md, the desktop-memory claims, the state docs, the docs/canon/ documents. Block decisions, 6 rows: the 85 memory copies and the 57 legacy worktree docs are not 142 rows, so each block gets one row proposing a decision.

The worklist's columns: id (stable, cite it in verdicts); surface (the file the claim is asserted in, file-level, with tiers 1 and 4 carrying it in the section heading and tiers 2, 3, 5 and B naming it per row with file:line where the line is load-bearing); claim (quoted verbatim as that surface states it, with ellipsis marking removed connective text only, never a qualifier); kind — intent (a claim about what the user wanted) or state (a claim about what exists, what a number is, what the code does), the distinction deciding what can settle it, since intent is settled only in the corpus and state only in git, code, data or run output; check (something runnable — a CQ corpus search, a git command, or a code path with line numbers, never "see the audit"); audit prior (CANON_AUDIT.md's verdict where one exists, marked as one agent's opinion and carrying no weight, with — meaning the audit never covered the claim); and status, every row starting unreviewed, changed only by the user.

The CQ corpus search, defined once per session in bash or PowerShell: it reads docs/canon/raw/user_turns_all.jsonl, matches a regex case-insensitively against each turn's text, and prints the corpus line number, the timestamp and the first 400 characters — the line number being what a verdict cites. rg is not on the bash PATH on this machine, so checks must not assume it. Zero hits is a real result and must be reported as such; it is not proof the user never said it.

Two things that will bite whoever works the list. The corpus blackouts: the corpus is 1,304 turns, 2026-05-14 → 2026-08-13, and this list's rows were written against the 803 extant on 08-03; nothing survives before 05-14, and 05-16 → 05-26 and 05-29 → 06-26 hold zero turns, so a claim whose only support would sit in those windows returns zero hits by construction — that is cannot-determine, never unsupported. Not hypothetical: two quotes CANON_AUDIT.md cites with dates — "MY WORDS ARE THE CANON" (06-25) and "this is ONLY RAGAS" (06-25) — return zero hits, because 06-25 is inside the second blackout; they are [DOC] recoveries out of raw/desktop_docs_record.md presented alongside genuine [CHAT] quotes with no visual distinction. And the four data files are off limits: v3/data/questions.jsonl, gold100.jsonl, heldout100.jsonl and 10smoke.jsonl are not to be opened (2026-08-02), so rows whose natural check would open one are marked [user-gated] — propose the check, do not run it.

Tier 1 covers CLAUDE.md in 50 claims across six groups: 1a the banner and repo-layout claims, 1b session entry point and trust ordering, 1c the graphify rules, 1d hard rules, 1e the agent roster section, 1f the artefact-arm section. 20 of these carry an audit prior and 30 are new to this list — the file was rewritten on 2026-08-03, after the audit read it, and the rewrite added a whole epistemics layer that nothing has checked.

Tier 2 covers the 25 live laptop memory files in 70 claims, grouped as 2a MEMORY.md (the index — the part actually skimmed), 2b the behavioural entries (feedback_*), 2c the design and vocabulary entries, 2d the environment entries, 2e the results entries (where the numbers live). 18 carry an audit prior and 52 are new.

Tier 3 covers the 10 agent definitions in 50 claims, grouped as 3a present in all ten definitions, 3b the terminology rule (six definitions), 3c the metric-validity table declared binding (five definitions), 3d pre-registered bars and closed findings, 3e design claims propagated into enforced rules, 3f method and behaviour rules. 14 carry an audit prior and 36 are new, with a verified line-number warning: every line citation in CANON_AUDIT.md for this surface is off.

Tier 4 covers v3/README.md in 28 claims (W-R01…W-R28); the ## Decided heading is what puts the file here, because every line under it is asserted as ruled. The audit adjudicated 12 and 16 are new. Rows include the system-under-test claim (audit prior CONTRADICTS-USER), the arms-share-nothing claim, the ID-based deterministic backbone, the quarantine claims, the gold-100 draw (where project_benchmark_validity_caveats.md says the set actually run is 22/55/17/5/1, not the equal 20-per-type draw, so two live surfaces describe the same file incompatibly), the shared-k / retrieval-budget rule, the haiku judge, the split telemetry, the provenance decision with no seed and no git-sha (CONTRADICTS-USER against his 07-16 traceability turn), the qwen generator claim (STALE, contested), the thin fixed RAG pipe, the lucene and vector build claims, the question-id minting, and the Still-open list. W-R10 is resolved — the claim is gone.

Tier 5 covers everything inert until someone opens it, in 40 rows carrying 53 audit claims: 5a v3/artefact/DESIGN.md + MODEL_CONTRACTS.md (15 rows — the audit's finding here was that staleness is not the main problem, unapproved content written as settled is); 5b desktop-memory claims (12 rows covering 30 audit claims, including W-E16, the one row holding the 19 entries the audit passed as an un-itemised list, which is itself the batch verdict REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md forbids); 5c the state docs (8 rows); 5d the docs/canon/ documents themselves (5 rows — CANON_AUDIT.md's own counts, its undifferentiated presentation of [DOC] and [CHAT] quotes, docs/canon/README.md's no-file-outranks-another claim against CLAUDE.md's attribution gate, its corpus figures, and this worklist in its entirety).

Block decisions, 6 rows. W-B01 docs/canon/raw/desktop_memory/ (53 files): review the 12 adjudicated claims and nothing else, since these are copies and the originals are live on the desktop where they still auto-load. W-B02 docs/canon/raw/laptop_memory/ (32 files): do not review, redundant with Tier 2, which reviews the live originals at the path that actually auto-loads. W-B03 and W-B04, the two pre-v3 worktree checkouts (27 and 30 files): rule the whole tree superseded or delete the worktree — they carry AGENTS.md files, exactly the shape an agent picks up by accident, and one already carries its own quarantine notice. W-B05 the 5 in-repo docs/state/*.md plus 11 OneDrive state docs (16 files): freeze as dated records and review only where a live surface declares one binding. W-B06 v3/output/ (130+ dirs): not interpretation — this is state, and it is the evidence other rows are checked against — with DATA_README.md the exception, agent-written prose declared binding by five agent definitions.
